newsitem.title: FRENCH POLYNESIA: Greenpeace expulsion from French N-site annulled.
newsitem.headline: Greenpeace expulsion from French N-site annulled.

text.p: A court in French Polynesia has annulled a 15-month-old expulsion order against Greenpeace founder David McTaggart for trying to stop nuclear tests in the South Pacific, justice sources said on Tuesday.

The Papeete court ruled that the expulsion order, enforced after McTaggart sailed into an exclusion zone around the testing site, was illegal because it applied only to French Polynesia while it should have applied to France and all its territories.
Legal sources said Monday's ruling would allow the veteran anti-nuclear activist to return to French Polynesia and opened the possibility of him claiming damages from the French state.

McTaggart was flown to Paris and on to London after French navy commandos boarded his protest ship in a 12-nautical mile exclusion zone around the Mururoa atoll test site on September 27 last year, three weeks after the first blast in France's final series of nuclear tests.
The navy had earlier seized three other Greenpeace protest ships, including the environmental group's flagship Rainbow Warrior, amid a storm of international protests against the tests.
France concluded the tests last January and has since signed a test ban treaty.
